lessons.title: MFA enrollment failed: inspect the device state
lessons.prompt: Teach a precise diagnostic case with title "MFA ENROLLMENT FAILED: CHECK DEVICE STATE". Premise "A cancelled setup can leave an unassigned virtual device; identify it before changing permissions." Main left short error document "iam:DeleteVirtualMFADevice" / "Explicit Deny during setup". A labelled illustration "Possible cause" shows cancelled phone-enrollment flow leaving device record "Created, not assigned". A magnifier leads to real checks "ListVirtualMFADevices" then two branches: "Unassigned device with matching ARN" -> administrator cleanup "DeleteVirtualMFADevice" -> "Enroll and verify the new device"; other branch "Assigned device or different evidence" -> "Investigate the actual policy and device state". Make administrator cleanup clearly operate on the unassigned record, not an enrolled user's working factor. Lower explanatory note "Do not remove MFA protection to solve a stale-device problem." Support "Confirm the device ARN and assignment state first." No terminalcommands, no fixedstepsnumbering, no claim this is the only cause. Beautiful modest phone, document, magnifier and role pictograms on open navy, a grounded evidence path rather than generic equal cards.

lessons.title: Choose a regional STS endpoint deliberately
lessons.layout: regional architecture and explicit endpoint selection
lessons.prompt: Title "STS: CHOOSE THE REGIONAL ENDPOINT". Premise "Select the credential-issuance endpoint explicitly and align it with the workload's Region." Main architecture two small meaningful region boundaries, not a globe infographic. Workload "Application • eu-west-1" sends "AssumeRole" to "sts.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com" within eu-west-1; response arrow "Temporary credentials" returns to application. Small alternate region eu-central-1 contains another STS endpoint; caption "Regional endpoints support fault-isolation design; failover must be designed." Below show SDK/configuration document with annotated fields "Region" and "STS endpoint selection" / "Verify the SDK's effective configuration." Useful side annotation "Regional STS tokens are valid across AWS Regions." Clarify "Endpoint selection does not grant resource permissions or extend credential expiry." A modest legacy-endpoint note "Global endpoint routing has changed; do not assume every request is served in us-east-1." No universalglobalrouting claim, no SDK-specific defaults, no forcedcardsequence, no table or mandatory footer. Use restrained faint network topology background only in empty regions, dark solid behind text.

lessons.title: AuthFailure: check token region compatibility
lessons.layout: observed error and two corrective alternatives
lessons.prompt: Title "AUTHFAILURE: CHECK TOKEN COMPATIBILITY". Premise "A temporary token's Region compatibility can differ from its permissions and expiry." Upper left application using temporary credentials -> opt-in Region endpoint "EC2 API • opt-in Region" -> error document "AuthFailure" / "Credentials could not be validated". Label this "One possible cause: a global-endpoint token with limited Region compatibility." Main evidence checks with magnifier: "Check expiry and the complete credential set" plus "Identify the STS endpoint that issued the token" plus "Confirm the target Region is enabled". Corrective alternatives below separated by OR: cyan "Request fresh credentials from a regional STS endpoint" and violet "Configure global-endpoint token compatibility for all Regions, then obtain fresh credentials". Clearly says freshcredentials inboth. Small explanatory caption "Changing compatibility does not rewrite tokens already issued." No claim every AuthFailure is compatibility, no claim allglobaltokensalwaysv1, no sessiontimeextension. Teach as an annotated failure case with actual source/request/evidence, not default numbered grid.

lessons.title: External ID binds the vendor request to its customer
lessons.prompt: Title "EXTERNAL ID: BIND THE CUSTOMER CONTEXT". Premise "A multi-tenant vendor includes a unique customer identifier when it assumes a customer's role." Architecture with vendor service in center, Customer A role right, Customer A and Customer B input requests left. The vendor maintains mapping "Customer A → A-7F2" and "Customer B → B-9C4" (illustrative values). Customer A legitimate route "AssumeRole + ExternalId A-7F2" to Customer A role trust check "Trusted vendor principal AND sts:ExternalId = A-7F2". Label matchingroute "External-ID condition matches; all other checks still apply". A clearly different Customer B request targeting A role -> vendor uses B'sown ID "ExternalId B-9C4" -> blocked "Customer context mismatch". Do not show customerB choosingA'sID; vendor assigns and binds unique IDs. Small readable note "External ID is not a secret and does not replace the trusted principal." Below role-to-approvedreportsbucket "Role permissions still control resource access." No greenoverallALLOW, no JSON. Compelling crisp tenant-colored arrows and boundary teaching story, quiet navy.

lessons.title: Assume the role, then call with its credentials
lessons.layout: cross-account issuance and resource use architecture
lessons.prompt: Title "CROSS-ACCOUNT ACCESS: ASSUME, THEN USE". Premise "The target role's temporary credentials become the identity used for the resource request." Clear Account A boundary left with developer role; Account B boundary right with ReportReaderRole and reports S3bucket. Center STS outside accountboundaries logically "AWS STS". Caller sends "AssumeRole: target role ARN" to STS; service checks source policy "Allows sts:AssumeRole on target ARN" and target trust policy "Trusts the approved caller". STS returns temporarycredential document to caller "Access key ID + secret access key + session token". Then a separate cyan request route FROM caller using newcredentialdocument to Account B S3 "Read report as assumed-role session". Highlight "Role permissions and other applicable policies govern the read." Sourceidentity not directlybucketsuccess. Modest exampleidentity label "arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/ReportReaderRole/session" may omitfullARN iftext too small use "Assumed-role session: ReportReaderRole/session" instead. Teach three responsibilities sourcepermission,targettrust,resourceauthorization. No vague sts arrows that implyresource datareturns STS; objectresponse backcaller. No mandatory footer; fit explanation adjacent to mechanisms.

lessons.title: Role session duration depends on how it is issued
lessons.prompt: Title "ROLE SESSIONS: CHECK THE DURATION LIMIT". Premise "AssumeRole lifetime is constrained by the role setting and the way the caller obtains the session." Diagram top modest role configuration "Maximum session duration: 4 hours (example)" beside requestdocument "DurationSeconds: 7200" -> temporarysessiontimeline "2-hour session" labelled "Within this role's configured limit". Bottom separate rolechaining architecture "Existing role session" -> "Assume another role" -> clock "Role chaining: maximum 1 hour". Add example "Requesting 2 hours through role chaining fails even when the target role allows 4 hours." Small meaningful detail "AssumeRole generally supports 15 minutes up to the configured role maximum (up to 12 hours)." Clear "The requested lifetime is not a guarantee of continued permission." No claim every STSAPI same durations, no claim EC2serviceassumption alwayshas1hrchaining, no universal1hrtemporarycredentials. Distinct matched numeric example and chain mechanism with clocks, modest pictograms and purposeful orange/cyan.

Two compact upper credential paths from EC2metadata: violet "IMDSv1 retrieval" -> credentialdocument -> signed AWS APIrequest context "ec2:RoleDelivery = 1.0"; cyan "IMDSv2 retrieval" -> separatedocument -> signedAPIrequestcontext "ec2:RoleDelivery = 2.0". These credentials go to one abstract resourcepolicygate "Example policy check: reject delivery below 2.0" with redblocked1.0 and neutral "Passes this check" for2.0.
